# Book of the Soul

[-won]derful and too high; I cannot grasp it: O **GOD**, Your thoughts—how great is the sum of them! If I should count them, they would be more in number than the sand of the sea. Thus we also read in *Job 11*: Do you think that you know as much as God knows, and that you could perfectly achieve everything as the Almighty does? He is higher than heaven; what will you do? Deeper than hell; what can you know? Longer than the earth, and broader than the sea. There has never been anyone who has fully learned it, and there never shall be anyone who might fathom it, for his mind is richer than any sea, and his word deeper than any abyss (*Sirach 1 & 24*). <note>original Latin: "Quæ igitur Deus occulta esse voluit, non sunt scrutanda, quæ autem manifesta fecit, non sunt negligenda, ne in illis illicitè curiosi, & in istis damnabiliter inveniamur ingrati."</note> *Therefore, those things which God willed to be hidden are not to be scrutinized; however, those things which he has made manifest are not to be neglected, lest we be found illicitly curious in the former, and culpably ungrateful in the latter,* (Ambrose, Book 1, *On the Calling of the Gentiles*, Chapter 7). For he who searches into things that are too difficult for him, it will become too hard for him (*Proverbs 25*). And the ways of the **LORD** remain unsearchable (*Romans 11*). Hence *Augustine* also says in Sermon 11, *On the Words of the Apostle*: <note>original Latin: "Disputare vis mecum, mirare mecum, & exclama: ô altitudo, ambo consentiant in pavore, ne in errore pereamus."</note> *You wish to dispute with me? Wonder with me, and exclaim: O the depth! Let us both agree in fear, lest we perish in error.*

Even *Paracelsus* <note>Philippus Aureolus Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim (1493–1541), a Swiss physician and alchemist who was often claimed as a spiritual forefather by radical groups.</note> himself—whom the <term>Rosicrucians</term> <note>A secret brotherhood of sages and alchemists whose manifestos had recently appeared in the early 17th century.</note> and <term>Enthusiasts</term> <note>From the German 'Schwärmer,' referring to radical religious groups who claimed direct personal revelation from the Holy Spirit.</note> may well call and recognize as their teacher and father—punished and censured such curiosity, when one wishes to investigate all things, even hidden secrets and what is to come; just as he writes in *The Mysteries of the Microcosm*, page 5: <note>original Latin: "Ne eorum stultiloquia curemus, qui plura de Deo loquuntur, quàm ipsis patefecerit, eumq; pariter intelligere volunt, à si fuissent ei à consilijs."</note> *Let us not heed the foolish talk of those who speak more of God than he has revealed to them, and who wish to understand him just as if they had been present at his councils.*

But there are many things hidden in Nature which we cannot investigate, to say nothing of the deep mysteries of spiritual matters; as *Pliny* teaches in Book 2, Chapter 96 and Book 32, Chapter 11: <note>original Latin: "multa sunt in naturæ majestate penitus abdita;"</note> *many things are deeply hidden within the majesty of nature;* With which also agrees...

# About the Rose Garden.

<note>original Latin: "Multa sunt in orbe sublunari, quae acie humana mentis pervestigari nequeunt, humana enim sapientia est, quædam æquo animo nesciri velle : Si autem cuncta in rerum naturâ exquisitè perquirere nec facile est nec possibile, ut cum Platone loquar lib. 7. de legibus. sed intellectus noster etiam in manifestissimis caecutit, ut ait Arist. 2. Metaph. 1. multò minus cuncta mysteria rimari, futura scire, & exquisitè ac perfectè omnes res cognoscere valemus."</note>
*Many things exist in the sublunary world <note>The "sublunary world" refers to the earthly realm below the moon, which in medieval science was considered subject to change and decay, unlike the perfect heavens.</note> which cannot be investigated by the sharp edge of the human mind; for it is a part of human wisdom to be willing to remain ignorant of certain things with a calm spirit. If, then, it is neither easy nor possible to search out everything in the nature of things with such precision (to speak with Plato in Book 7 of the Laws), and our intellect is blind even in the most obvious matters (as Aristotle says in the second book of his Metaphysics, Chapter 1), we are much less able to pry into all mysteries, to know the future, or to know all things with exquisite and perfect accuracy.*

And even though **Cardano** <note>Gerolamo Cardano (1501–1576), an Italian polymath known for his work in mathematics, medicine, and philosophy.</note> presumed that he could give an account of all natural things and point out their causes, he did not fulfill or achieve this in his actual work, <note>original Latin: "unde etiam reprehenditur à Scaligero Ex 218. f. 8."</note> *wherefore he is even rebuked by Scaliger in Exercise 218, folio 8.* For we do not even know how our own speaking, laughing, or sleeping happens—as **Luther** says in the <term>Church Postil<gloss>A collection of sermons for the Sundays and festivals of the church year</gloss></term> for Trinity Sunday, on the Epistle, page 139. If we perform and feel these natural works daily, how should we then have knowledge of all other natural things and be able to point out and give their causes? Or how should we be able to learn of and search out the Divine mysteries and what is yet to happen in the future? Oh, the great blindness and vanity! No one sees what God intends to do, and no man notices the weather that is at hand; He can do much that no one expects, and who can speak of it or endure it when He judges? But such things are too far from the eyes of these three, and when a crude man hears of it, he remains in his folly and in his error (*Sirach 16:19-20*).

Although the new <term>Enthusiasts<gloss>A derogatory term used at the time for radical reformers who claimed direct, personal inspiration from the Holy Spirit</gloss></term> and <term>Chiliasts<gloss>Those who believe in a literal 1,000-year earthly reign of Christ (the Millennium)</gloss></term> may pretend and argue that it has been revealed to them above other men by the Holy Spirit through "the anointing," these are nevertheless mere nullities which no sensible person recognizes or accepts as true. For God does not wish to deal with us without <term>means<gloss>In theology, "means" refer to the physical tools God uses to communicate, such as the Bible (the Word) and the Sacraments, rather than direct mystical revelation</gloss></term>; rather, He speaks to us in these last days through His Word (*Hebrews 1*). God's Word has not only had to suffer great <term>persecution</term> <note>original Latin: *persecution*</note> from the enemies of Christ and public enemies of the Church, but has also at all times had to experience and suffer manifold <term>depravation</term> <note>original Latin: *depravation*; meaning the corruption or distortion of the text and its meaning</note> from false teachers, heretics, and visionaries. Cerdon and Marcion recognized and confessed only the Gospel of Luke as God's Word <note>Tertullian, *On Prescription against Heretics*, at the end</note>. ## Book of Heroes

<note>original: *Heldenbuch*; this likely refers to a specific section of the work or a collection of "heroes of the faith" or "champions of doctrine."</note>

here the same <note>referring to the Book of Revelation</note> is *solidly and vigorously* <note>original: *solidè & nervosè*</note> defended and explained. Some have doubted whether *John* the Apostle and Evangelist wrote this book? However, the ancient Church Fathers provide a thorough and detailed account of this, especially *Melito, Bishop of Sardis; Theophilus of Antioch; and Justin Martyr; who were all* <note>original: σύγχρονοι (*synchronoi*)</note> *almost contemporaries [of the apostles], and did not extend their lives beyond the sixtieth year after the death of John the Evangelist* <note>original: *qui omnes σύγχρονοι ferè fuerunt, & ultra annum sexagesimum post Johannis Evangelistæ obitum, vitam non protraxerunt*</note>, and they testify that *John* wrote this book on *Patmos*; likewise, *Dionysius the Areopagite, Irenaeus, Tertullian, Hippolytus, Athanasius, Cyprian, Jerome, Augustine, Ambrose, Theophilus, Apollonius, Origen, Primasius, Philastrius*, and many others teach the same. Furthermore, right at the beginning, a particular conformity with the *Gospel* and the first *Epistle of John* reveals itself: This is the Revelation, he says in *Revelation 1:1–2*:

> [The Revelation] of Jesus Christ, which God gave to him, to show his servants what must shortly come to pass; and he signified it and sent it by his angel to his servant *John*, who bore witness to the word of God and the testimony of Jesus Christ, of all things that he saw.

He speaks in almost the same words, and with the same meaning and intent, in the *Gospel Chapter 21:24*:

> This is the disciple who testifies of these things and has written these things, and we know that his testimony is true.

And he also begins his first *Epistle* with such words:

> That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we have looked upon and our hands have touched of the Word of Life—that which we have seen and heard, we proclaim to you, so that you also may have fellowship with us; and our fellowship is with the Father and with his Son, **JESUS CHRIST.**

Furthermore, *Erasmus* in his *Annotations, page 782 and following*, belittled this book not a little, *asserting that there was no Apostolic majesty within it* <note>original: *eiꝙ nullam inesse Apostolicam majestatem asseruit*</note>.

*Paræus* <note>David Pareus (1548–1622) was a prominent Reformed (Calvinist) theologian and professor at Heidelberg.</note> also writes this in his defense of the <term>Neustadt Bible: a Calvinist-leaning German translation of the Bible published in 1579 to compete with Luther’s translation</term>, page 103. Indeed, it is even more than that: Christ wishes not only for all sorts of people, but for each and every individual to come to Him, just as God wishes that each and every one be saved. But this is not in the same sense of the will. For He wishes even the unrepentant to come to Him—that is, He earnestly commands them to repent and takes pleasure in their obedience and welfare (even though He well knows that it does not please His Father to give them repentance and faith, *Matthew 11 and 13*). This is what the scholars call the <term>will of command and approval: *voluntatem præcepti & adprobationis*</term>. But to the elect, He calls outwardly and simultaneously works inwardly so that they come, for they are His sheep given to Him by the Father. Therefore, they are powerfully drawn through the Word and the Holy Spirit so that they believe and are saved, which is called the <term>will of efficacy: *voluntas efficaciæ*</term>.

We read something similar in *Renneccius* <note>Jacob Renneccius (1572–1611) was a Lutheran theologian who often wrote against Calvinism.</note> in his *Golden Chain* <note>original Latin: *Aurea Catena*</note> <margin>q 24. p. 167.</margin>. But these are such abominable paradoxes that heaven and earth might be horrified by them. For God threatens to punish all those who deal in such hypocrisy and deceit, <note>original Latin: *& aliud clausum in corde, aliud promptum in ore habent*</note> "having one thing hidden in the heart and another ready on the tongue." He wishes for us to walk without blemish, to do what is right, and to speak the truth from the heart (*Psalm 15*). How then could He Himself be so double-tongued, saying one thing and not meaning it? ### §. 8. Shall not the prophecy of *Malachi, chapter 4,* be fulfilled, stating that Elijah is to return?

Just as the Papists <term>Papists: a polemical term for Roman Catholics</term> publicly propagate and spread these unscriptural dreams throughout worthy Christendom—claiming that **Enoch** and **Elijah** shall return before the Antichrist appears and Judgment Day approaches, in order to preserve the elect in the faith of Christ and convert the Jews <note>Citing Robert Bellarmine, *On the Roman Pontiff*, Book 3, Ch. 6; Martin Becanus, Vol. 1 and 2; and Ferdinandus Velosillus.</note>—so also do the new **Chiliasts** <term>Chiliasts: those who believe in a literal 1,000-year earthly reign of Christ</term> teach that the prophecy of *Malachi chapter 4* concerning the return of Elijah shall be fulfilled. **Paulus Felgenhauer** <note>A 17th-century German mystic and controversialist</note> writes in his *Mirror of the Times* <note>original title: *Zeitspiegel*</note> at sections *A. ij.* and *B. iij.* that this must happen before the Kingdom of Glory begins here on Earth with Christ and His fellow citizens. 

However, who this "Elijah" is supposed to be can easily be concluded and gathered from their own words. For Felgenhauer does not want it understood as referring to **Luther** (*Mirror of the Times, section B. iij.*), nor even the Angel in *Revelation 14:6* bearing the eternal Gospel (*section F. i.*). Instead, he forces the interpretation onto **himself** and his Chiliastic associates. We likewise read in **Nagelius** <note>Paul Nagel, a mathematician and astronomer who predicted the end of the world</note> in his treatise *On the New Philosophy* (*section K. j.*) that they wish to be understood as being the "Two Witnesses" mentioned in *Revelation 11*.

For Felgenhauer writes thus in the *Mirror of the Times* at section *A. ij.*:
> Since no one can see this light except the elect, it has been given to me through the Spirit of God that I, in His grace, can not only see and recognize for myself the terrible darkness and great, thick, black clouds that stand before the sun, but also point them out to others—indeed, to the whole world—with my fingers, if it were possible.

# From the Rose Garden #

It is written in 2 Kings 17 that Israel was led away from its land into Assyria, and Samaria was occupied by heathens.

We certainly acknowledge and freely admit—as long as the literal understanding <note>The "literal understanding" (*Buchstabische Verstand*) refers to the historical events as they actually happened, a cornerstone of Lutheran biblical interpretation.</note> and the histories remain pure and unadulterated—that Judah and Jerusalem can indeed be types <note>original Latin: *typi*</note> and archetypes <note>The author uses the phrase *impropriè sic dicti*, meaning "improperly so-called," to suggest these are spiritual metaphors rather than the primary historical meaning.</note> in a spiritual interpretation of the Christians and believers in the New Testament. Upon these believers, because of their overwhelming sin, punishment and destruction will draw near and will not fail to arrive; for God is a righteous God who threatens daily. If one will not repent, he has whetted his sword and bent his bow, and has aimed deadly projectiles; he has prepared his arrows for destruction, as seen in Psalm 7. Therefore, with a repentant and remorseful heart, we should submit to God’s rod <note>To "fall into God's rod" is an idiom meaning to accept His discipline or punishment with humility.</note> so that he might graciously turn the well-deserved punishment away from us; for he is gracious, merciful, long-suffering, and of great kindness, and he relents from doing harm, according to Jonah 4.

When Isaiah 9 prophesies of the birth of the Holy Christ—how the faithful, "Amen" God <note>A reference to God as the ultimate truth or "The Amen" (Revelation 3:14).</note> will certainly one day fulfill what he has promised and pledged regarding the Messiah and Savior of the world—the **Anonymous Author** in *The Sound of the Prophetic Trumpet* <note>original Latin: *Clangore Buccinae Propheticae*, a work by Paul Felgenhauer.</note> at section E. ij. rejects not only such a literal understanding, but also the general consensus of the entire Christian Church. He claims that it actually belongs to the **age of the Holy Spirit** <note>original Latin: *seculum Spiritus Sancti*</note> or to the **Millennial Kingdom** <term>Chiliastic: referring to the "Chiliasmus" or the belief in a literal 1,000-year reign of Christ on earth before the final judgment.</term>. According to him, the rod—which is not the rod of the Law, but of the persecution and great tyranny of the godless against the believers because of their unrepentant lives—will be broken. He argues that all war, with its turmoil and blood-stained garments, will be burned and consumed with fire. Then the child who is born to us, and the son who is given to us, will become great in his dominion (which is upon his shoulder) once he has brought all war to an end.

As Paul explains in **1 Corinthians 15**, the Holy Christ has overcome these, and made a public spectacle of them in a triumph through himself, according to **Colossians 2**.

The Prophet also indicates the manner in which such a war was begun and the victory and triumph obtained, saying: *as in the time of Midian*. For just as the valiant hero Gideon, with three hundred men, fought a great battle and overcame his enemies (**Judges 7**), so Christ has slain all spiritual enemies without external protection or troops of soldiers <note>original Latin: *absque externis præsidiis & militum copiis*</note>.

Secondly: just as Gideon achieved the triumph when they broke the empty jars, so Christ had to die and sacrifice his body on the altar of the cross (**Ephesians 5**). He was meant to strip the devil of his power (**Luke 11**) and plunder and storm the gates of hell (**Matthew 16:3** <note>Likely a reference to Matthew 16:18 regarding the gates of hell, or a specific commentary tradition.</note>).

Thirdly: just as Gideon struck his enemies through the sound of trumpets, so Christ has overcome death, the devil, and hell through the sound and resonance of the Gospel trumpets, and has redeemed us from all enemies who hate us (**Luke 1**). One may read further on this in **Luther**, in the Jena edition, Volume 3, folio 178.

[God takes] our ignominy and shame, our sickness and pains from us, and throws or lays them upon His Son *Isaiah 53.* And in exchange, He gives us His heavenly glory and majesty: so that we may well glory with the Apostle Paul and say: "herein God commends His love toward us, that Christ died for us while we were yet sinners" *Romans 5.*

Furthermore, it is also a Day of Wrath because the **Holy** Christ, in righteous wrath and zeal, overcame His enemies in the bloody battle and displayed them publicly. It is also finally a Day of Wrath for the stubborn Jews and all the godless, who neither respect nor consider Christ's merit, but persist and harden in their sins without shame or repentance. For He did not die for the elect alone—as the Calvinists foam and fume <note>original: *geyfern vnd eyfern*, a play on words suggesting both drooling/foaming and being overly zealous</note> (*Zanchius, Volume 2, Miscellanies, page 117; Piscator, Volume 2, Theological Disputations, pages 129, 130, 131; Spindler in his Necessary Report, page 263*)—but for each and every person *1 John 1.* And He wills that they should all be converted, believe in Him, and be saved *John 3; Ezekiel 3, 18, and 33; 1 Timothy 2.* 

But if a person will not be converted, but instead treads Christ’s merit underfoot, then the Lord God performs a "strange work" <note>original: *frembd Werck*, a theological concept referring to Isaiah 28:21, where God's judgment is seen as "strange" compared to His "proper" nature of love</note> and, instead of love, lets His wrath—and instead of mercy, His strict justice—take its course and happen. Then it is as Isaiah laments and says: they do not hide their nature <note>original: *Wesen*</note>, and they boast of their sin.

# Hero-Book

There are three books, each one within the other, and none without the other: the first great book is the macrocosm <note>literally "the great world"</note> with all its creatures; the second is Jesus Christ; the third is Man. In these you have the three physical, temporal persons: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. These three lead you to the three eternal Heavenly Persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—one eternal God. For Father, Son, and Holy Spirit is God, just as the Son, Father, and Holy Spirit is the Word. In the heavenly spiritual realm, they are essentially one and undivided. In the earthly bodily realm, they are divided according to their natures, offices, and persons, such that the Father is one person—who dwells bodily in the Son—and the Son and the Holy Spirit are distinct persons. Outside of Christ Jesus, who died on the Cross, there is no God nor any Person; He is everything, He is the whole and the complete; He is Father, Son, and Holy Spirit in a heavenly sense (therefore He is called Jesus as the Spirit) and He is Father, Son, and Holy Spirit in a bodily, earthly sense (therefore He is called Christ as the Word).

*And in Chapter 3* he says: there are three temporal, bodily persons—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—and yet only one Christ. And furthermore in *chapter 4*: In the beginning, God created, made, and brought forth the Word, which is Wisdom, and spoke, "**Let there be light**" <note>original Latin: "fiat lux"</note>. This Word or Wisdom is God Himself—one Godhead, but two persons. Thus, **GOD** and His Word, His Wisdom, are a pair <note>The German "Gemahl" suggests a spouse or consort, a common theme in Sophiology where Wisdom is the feminine counterpart to the Divine.</note> born out of Himself, as she herself says: "**I came forth from the mouth of the Most High**" <note>original Latin: "ex ore altissimi prodij"</note>; and He says to Wisdom, to Christ: "**Today I have begotten thee**" <note>original Latin: "ego hodie genui te"</note> Psalm 2; "**I begot thee before the morning star**" <note>original Latin: "ante luciferum genui"</note> Psalm 110. God and His consort, His Wisdom, created everything and are one perfect Creator. *And in Chapter 5*: God is without a will, or has no will **absolutely in Himself** <note>original Latin: "absolutè per se"</note>, when considered **without any creature** <note>original Latin: "sine creatura"</note>. Likewise, the creature is also without a will, without affections, **outside of God** <note>original Latin: "extra Deum"</note> or **without God** <note>original Latin: "sine Deo"</note>; each by itself is nothing at all. Eternity is not entirely without time, and time is nothing without eternity; however, one should not attempt to contemplate God without the creature.

# Book of Heroes

...to speak, nor has a righteous teacher ever used such or similar words. For as **Cicero** says in the second book of *The Nature of the Gods*: *it is an evil and impious habit to argue against the gods, whether it is done in earnest or as a pretense.* <note>original Latin: "mala enim & impia consuetudo est, ait Cicero lib. 2. de Nat. Deor. contra Deos disputandi, sive examine hoc fiat sive simulate." The word "examine" is likely a transcription error for "ex animo" (sincerely).</note>

Fourthly, Weigel heaps and piles up various errors in his fifth chapter. For God, he says, is: 
1. Will-less or without a will without the **creature** <note>The "creature" (Creatur) refers to anything created by God, including humans.</note>.
2. The creature is without will without God.
3. Neither God nor the creature is anything for itself, *on its own*, but rather nothing at all.
4. Eternity is not entirely without time.
5. Time is nothing without eternity.
6. The will-less God received a will through the temporal creature.
7. The will of God and the creature is only one and not two wills.

...we must speak of God in this way: that He has His Divine will, <note>original Latin: *quicquid enim convenit enti, quatenus ens, illud maximè & perfectissimè competit primo enti, quod est DEus, ut ajunt Philosophi:* "for whatever belongs to being, insofar as it is being, belongs most greatly and perfectly to the first being, which is God, as the philosophers say."</note> And He did not receive such a Will in time from the **creatures** <note>The "creature" (Creatur) refers to anything created by God, including humans.</note>, according to the blasphemy of **Weigel** <note>Valentin Weigel (1533–1588), a mystical theologian whose views were seen as heretical by orthodox Lutherans.</note>, but has had it from eternity; and we have received the will and everything we have—body and soul—from Him, and not He from us. For with such a distinction, all *objections* that might be raised against this can be refuted and settled.

Such perfection is lacking in the sun and its radiance, for the sun has its own clarity for itself, and the radiance for itself, even though the radiance receives its nature from the sun. However, through the envy of the Devil, sin entered into mankind, according to *Wisdom 2*, and was inherited by us all, according to *Romans 5.* *The serpent was the plunderer of the divine image, a light-shunning beast,* as *Tertullian* wrote in *Against the Valentinians.* For God had commanded that they should not eat of the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden, *Genesis 3.* But the Devil persuaded our grandmother Eve with sugar-coated words, so that she set aside God's command and gazed upon the tree—that it was pleasant and lovely, and good to eat from, *Genesis 3, 4.* <note>original Latin: "hoc est, considerat diligenter, secundum Rupertum, intuetur curiosus, attendit, & judex eorum quae audierat esse vult"</note> *That is, she considers it diligently; according to Rupert, she looks at it curiously, pays attention, and wishes to be the judge of those things she had heard.* Thereupon, the *external and internal senses* were immediately corrupted and spoiled; and after they had eaten of the forbidden fruit, the eyes of them both were opened, and they recognized that they were naked. *Indeed they were naked before,* says *Ambrose* in *Volume 1 of his book on Paradise, chapter 13, on my page 64,* *but not without the covering of virtues: they were naked because of the simplicity of their character and because their nature knew not the cloak of deceit; now, however, the human mind is veiled with many layers of pretense.*

### Of the Rose Garden. 136

But if man, through the Devil’s prompting, ate from the forbidden tree—as Moses clearly states in Genesis 3—then evil certainly did not originate from man, nor did it initially spring from his heart; nor was man seduced by himself, as **Weigelius** <note>Valentin Weigel (1533–1588), a mystic whose ideas that evil was an internal necessity in man were considered heretical by the author.</note> fanatically speculates, nor was he himself the "tree in the middle of the garden." For the man who was created according to God’s image is one thing, the tree in the middle of the garden from which the man eats is another, and the Devil who seduces the man is yet another.

And although **Weigelius** wishes to confirm his opinion by pointing to the evil desire—which is innate to us humans after the Fall—and thereby conclude that just as evil is in all people and springs from the heart, so it must also have been in the first man and come from within him: such a conclusion is nothing other than a **perverse and empty inference** <note>original Latin: "perversa & vana illatio"</note>. For there is a great difference **between the state of innocence and the state of guilt or transgression** <note>original Latin: "inter statum innocentiae & nocentiae seu transgressionis"</note>. Before the Fall, man was good and formed according to God’s image; but after the Fall, he immediately fathered children **in his own likeness, after his image** <note>original Hebrew: בִּדְמוּתוֹ כְּצַלְמוֹ (bidmuto ketsalmo)</note>, who were like his own image (Genesis 5:3). Before the Fall, there was no evil desire or inclination toward evil in man. Instead, the Devil infused evil into him with sweet words, as Eve herself laments and says: **"The serpent deceived me"** <note>original Hebrew: הַנָּחָשׁ הִשִּׁיאַנִי (hanachash hishiani)</note>. But after the Fall, we are conceived and born in sin (Psalm 51). And every imagination and striving is evil from youth (Genesis 6 & 8). For Adam did not sin for himself alone, but his disobedience—as Paul says in Romans 5—is inherited by us all, **because he was the root of the human race** <note>original Latin: "quia radix fuit generis humani"</note>. Nevertheless, the **Photinians** <note>A term used here to describe the Socinians, a group that denied the Trinity and the doctrine of original sin.</note> un-Christianly deny this despite the clear, bright grounds of Scripture, as seen in **Osterodt** <note>Christoph Osterodt (d. 1611), a prominent Socinian writer.</note> in his *Report*, chapter 15. Therefore, the good cannot exist within him at the same time. Hence **Justin Martyr** <note>An early Christian apologist (c. 100–165 AD) who wrote defenses of the faith.</note> says in his *Letter to Zenas and Serenus*: <note>original Latin: *Mera caro sumus, nec quicquam boni inhabitat bonis: advocandus est igitur ad nostri curam medicus: sic enim fugato morbo continget sanitas.* Note: "bonis" is likely a transcription error for "nobis" (in us).</note> "We are mere flesh, and nothing good dwells in us; therefore, a physician must be called to care for us; for only when the disease is driven out can health follow."

Thirdly: where death is, there is certainly no vital power; <note>original Latin: *ubi mors ibi nulla potentia vitalis*</note> "where death is, there is no power of life." But the human being is dead in sins (Col. 2) and has died to all good works (Eph. 2). Therefore, life is not within him. If life is not within him, then Christ is also not in him, for Christ alone bears the glory and the name of being the "Life and the Resurrection" (John 11).

Fourthly: where Christ is, there is pure life and blessing, pure comfort and joy, much grace and mercy. In the natural human being, however, there is nothing else but pure wrath and disfavor, as St. Paul says: "we are by nature children of wrath" (Eph. 2). Therefore, Christ is also not in man by nature; <note>original Latin: *omnis enim homo naturaliter non peccator est, sed etiam totus peccatum, ait Chrysost. Dom. 1. Advent. hom. 25.*</note> "for every man by nature is not only a sinner, but is even entirely sin," says **Chrysostom** <note>John Chrysostom (c. 347–407 AD), a celebrated preacher and Archbishop of Constantinople.</note> in his 25th homily for the first Sunday of Advent. For all his actions are inclined toward evil, and through them, he deserves nothing else but pure wrath and disfavor (Rom. 5 & 6).

### Q. 6. Does the Fall into sin happen "substantially" or "essentially"?

Weigel suggests the Fall changed the very "stuff" of human nature.</term>. Furthermore, he claims that **regeneration** <term>Regeneration (Wiedergeburt): The spiritual rebirth of a person through grace.</term> is also an **accident** in that the will is given back to God, and yet it is also a substance, because Christ dwelling in us is not an accident but a substance; and in His flesh and blood we shall rise after our death, which is also a substance.

### Q. 3. Will Christ then return twice?

The new **Chiliasts** <term>Chiliasts: Also known as Millenarians; those who believe in a literal 1,000-year earthly reign of Christ.</term> are of the total hope that Christ will return twice; they call the first coming "Christ’s Revelation," but the other coming "Christ’s visible Future and Appearance." **Paulus Felgenhauer** <note>A controversial 17th-century Bohemian visionary and writer often at odds with Lutheran orthodoxy.</note> argues this in his *Mirror of the Times* under the letter *F*, which he intends to prove from *2 Thessalonians 1:7-9*. And the **anonymous author** says in *The Sound of the Prophetic Trumpet* <note>original Latin title: "Clangore Buccinæ Propheticæ"</note> under letter *B*: That there is a great difference between this last and first judgment. In the first judgment, described in *Daniel 7*, the **Ancient of Days** <note>A title for God the Father used in the Book of Daniel.</note> held the judgment; therefore, it can not unfairly be called the **judgment of the Father** <note>original Latin: "judicium patris"</note>. Although the Son—the **terrible word of Jehovah** <note>original Latin: "tremendum verbum Jehovæ"</note> mentioned in *Revelation 19*—carries out the execution and treads the **winepress of the fierce wrath of God** <note>A biblical metaphor for divine judgment, found here in Isaiah 63.</note>, the Father hands over the kingdom, all power, and dominion to the Son. While the Son has possessed these from eternity, he demonstrates them in **actuality** <note>original Latin: "in actu"</note> through the destruction of his enemies and the elevation of his believers and saints. In this *last* judgment, however, of which **Paul** speaks in *1 Corinthians 15*, and the Revelation, the Son hands over and delivers the kingdom back to the Father, so that God may be all in all. In the first judgment, heaven and earth remain standing; in this last judgment, heaven and earth flee and pass away—everything that is visible—and only the invisible remains.

Prophetic Literature, Letter B. <note>Likely a reference to the writings of Paul Nagel, mentioned on the previous page.</note> That the radiance of the Heavenly Paradise will fill the entire New Jerusalem, and just as Christ raised up the disciples in Matthew 17 <note>A reference to the Transfiguration, where Jesus appeared in glory to Peter, James, and John.</note> so that they could behold His glory, so He will also enlighten the believers here on earth during the 1,000 years in His worldly kingdom and open their eyes. Q 5. **Will Christ not then establish a new earthly paradise on earth and restore everything once again to the previous state that Adam had before the Fall?**

Just as the Papists <note>A common Reformation-era term for Roman Catholics.</note> dream that Paradise was not destroyed by the Great Flood but is still to be found today—see *Bellarmine, On the Grace of the First Man, Book 1, Chapter 14; Thomas Aquinas, Summa Theologica, Part 1, Question 102, Articles 2 and 3; Matthäus Felisius, On the Christian State, Disputation 17, Chapter 11, Page 258; Felicianus Capitonus, Catholic Explanations, Part 5, Page 28; Martinus Becanus, Works Volume 1, Chapter 14, Section 7, Page 608.* And they claim that **Enoch** and **Elijah** are preserved therein—see *Ferdinand Vellosillo, Remarks on Ambrose, Question 2, Folio 2.* 

In the same way, the new Chiliasts <term>Chiliasts: from the Greek 'chilioi' (thousand); those who believe in a literal 1,000-year earthly reign of Christ</term> also have their particular dreams and delays, claiming that Christ shall establish a new earthly paradise here on earth and restore and compel everything back into the previous state that **Adam** had before the Fall. This is exactly what the *Brothers of the Rose Cross* <note>original Latin: *Fratres Roseæ Crucis*; the Rosicrucians.</note> write in their *Confession, page 69*: "God has decreed that even before the end of the world, He will grant such truth, light, life, and glory as the first man lost in Paradise." 

But these are pure nullities, or it is *vanity of vanities* <note>original Latin: *vanitas vanitatum*</note>. For Paradise was nothing other than a beautiful, magnificent garden of pleasure, full of adornment and glory, from which it also takes its name from *Pardes* and *Parah* <note>original Hebrew: פרדס (orchard/paradise) and פרה (to be fruitful)</note>, *which is to say, a fertile myrtle, a certain storehouse of joy and pleasure* <note>original Latin: *hoc est fertilis myrtus, promtuarium quoddam fuer. lætitiæ ac voluptatis*</note>. In this world after the Fall, however, no person will live in such earthly paradisiacal joy; rather, we must pass through the valley of sorrow <note>original: *Jammerthal*; a reference to Psalm 84:6 (Psalm 48 in the author's citation)</note> and be brought into the Kingdom of God through much cross and tribulation (Acts 14). *For he who deserts God is justly deserted by God; because by hoping [to gain something while sinning], man sins, and by deserting the sinner, God preserves justice* <note>original Latin: *Qui enim deserit Deum, justè deseritur à DEO, quia sperens DEum homo peccat, deserens peccatorem DEus, justitiam servat*; from Fulgentius of Ruspe, *To Monimus*, Book 1, Chapter 13</note>.

# Book of Heroes

->*We are blessed, provided we relate all things to that life; yet in hope rather than in fact: and without hope, the whole life on earth is a false happiness and great misery.*<note>original Latin: "beati sumus, modo omnia ad illam vitam referamus; spe tamen potius quam re: & sine spe tota vita in terris falsa beatitudo & magna miseria est."</note><-

**Eleventhly**, if the believers do not rise again before the **Last Day** <term>Last Day: The final day of the world, marking the general resurrection of the dead and the final judgment of humanity.</term>, then they certainly cannot live for a thousand years—along with the others who are living and remaining—in all manner of joy and pleasure. Now, however, the Spirit of God clearly indicates
<margin>John 14:11, 12 <note>Though the text cites John, the description of the dead not waking "so long as the heavens remain" suggests the author intended to cite Job 14:11–12.</note></margin>

Therefore, what the new **Chiliasts** <term>Chiliasts: From the Greek 'chilioi' (thousand); those who believe Christ will return to establish a literal 1,000-year kingdom on earth before the end of the world.</term>—and in ancient times also **Lactantius** <note>Lactantius (c. 250 – c. 325) was an early Christian advisor to Constantine who held Millenarian views.</note> in his *Divine Institutes*, book 7, chapter 23—teach is false and incorrect: namely, that the believers shall rise from the dead and live here on earth in joy for 1,000 years. **Twelfthly**, if Christ intended to live here on earth with his fellow-citizens of the kingdom for 1,000 years in glory and joy, the believers would surely hold together beautifully in unity of faith and love. One would not need to doubt whether faith and the Christian Church were still present on earth. But Christ himself says in Luke 18: "When the Son of Man comes, do you think he will find faith on earth?" This is not because one should doubt the Church's survival—for the gates of hell shall not overcome it (Matthew 16)—but rather because of the great persecution and various heresies which eat away at their surroundings like **cancerous diseases** <note>original: "Krebs Kranckheiten" (literally, crab-diseases or cankers). Because of this, one may well lament and say—and truly at this very time—that the godly people have vanished from the land, and the righteous are no longer among the people (Micah 7).

Yes, come, dear LORD Jesus, and take us into your eternal kingdom, Amen. The grace of our LORD Jesus Christ be with you all, AMEN.
